title: Networking Domain 3: Monitoring, Documentation, HA & DR (19%)
overview: Covers SNMP/Syslog/NetFlow monitoring, network documentation, RPO/RTO disaster recovery metrics, and High Availability.

1.label: Network Monitoring: SNMP, Syslog, NetFlow & Packet Capture
1.what: Tools used to track device health, hardware alerts, event logs, and bandwidth usage across the enterprise.
1.exam_facts: SNMP (UDP 161 polling / UDP 162 Traps): Queries MIBs using OIDs. Always use SNMPv3 (adds encryption & authentication—v1/v2c send community strings in plain text!). Syslog (UDP 514): Centralizes event logs ranked by Severity 0 (Emergency) to 7 (Debug). NetFlow/sFlow/IPFIX: Analyzes traffic flows/bandwidth talkers without capturing full packet payloads.
1.troubleshoot: Set up a SPAN (Port Mirroring) port on a switch when you need to copy live traffic from one port to a Wireshark analyzer without interrupting the link.

2.label: Network Documentation, Baselines & Change Management
2.what: Standard operating records that let any technician understand how the network is built and spot abnormal behavior fast.
2.exam_facts: Logical Diagram (IP subnets, VLANs, routing protocols) vs Physical Diagram (cable runs, rack elevations, MDF/IDF patch panels). Performance Baseline: Captures normal CPU, memory, and bandwidth usage so you can prove when something is abnormal. Change Management: Requires risk assessment, rollback plan, and maintenance window approval before touching production configs.
2.troubleshoot: Always back up a switch/router's running-config (`copy run start` + TFTP/SCP backup) BEFORE applying firmware updates or ACL changes!

3.label: Disaster Recovery (DR) Metrics: RPO, RTO, MTTR & MTBF
3.what: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery metrics that define how much data a company can afford to lose and how fast systems must recover.
3.exam_facts: RPO (Recovery Point Objective): Maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time (e.g., hourly backups = 1-hour RPO). RTO (Recovery Time Objective): Maximum acceptable downtime after an outage. MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures): Average lifespan/reliability of hardware. MTTR (Mean Time To Repair): Average time to fix a broken component.
3.troubleshoot: If a mission-critical database requires near-zero RPO and RTO, standard nightly tape backups won't cut it—you need real-time synchronous replication and automated failover.

4.label: High Availability (HA), Redundancy & Recovery Sites
4.what: Eliminating Single Points of Failure (SPOF) across power, hardware, links, and physical facilities.
4.exam_facts: Active-Active (both units share traffic load simultaneously) vs Active-Passive (standby unit takes over only if primary fails via FHRP/CARP/VRRP). Cold Site (empty building/power only, cheapest, weeks to setup) vs Warm Site (racks & network gear ready, needs data restore) vs Hot Site (live mirror, instant failover, most expensive).
4.troubleshoot: True power redundancy requires dual PSUs plugged into SEPARATE UPS battery backups fed by SEPARATE electrical circuits/PDUs.
